top.title: The story that ended Trev Alberts’ Michigan AD tenure before it even began
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-USA TODAY Sports The story that ended Trev Alberts’ Michigan AD tenure before it even began appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michigan has decided not to hire Trev Alberts as the next athletic director. Michigan reversed course on the hire on Tuesday , even though there was a memorandum of understanding signed between the two sides. Now, the story that ended the Alberts’ tenure before it even began has come to light. David Covucci of FOIAball found a lawsuit that involved Trev Alberts, who was then the Nebraska AD. The lawsuit was filed in 2024 by Ashley Scoggin against the Nebraska Board of Regents, the school’s women’s basketball coach, and then-AD Alberts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “According to the lawsuit, during an away game, a student-manager duped a hotel employee into giving out a card key to assistant coach Chuck Love’s room. Two players used the card to enter Love’s room and filmed Scoggin in his bed. Presented with the video, head coach Amy Williams allegedly called a meeting and allowed the entire team to confront Scoggin over the relationship,” Covucci wrote. “Scoggin was initially suspended. Back in Nebraska, she was kicked off the team. Love was suspended with pay and allowed to quietly resign three months later. Alberts eventually agreed to pay Love $136,000 in severance. The lawsuit accuses Alberts of violating Scoggin’s civil rights after learning of the relationship by approving of her removal from the team, refusing to order an investigation, and encouraging her to leave the school.” The lawsuit led to two different depositions of Alberts, and some shocking details from the depositions came to light. First, he did not know he had been named vice chancellor at Nebraska. Meanwhile, he also gave some evasive answers about relationships between staff and students. “Faculty or Staff members are prohibited from engaging in any romantic relationship with an undergraduate student,” the Nebraska policy on consensual relationships reads. Alberts was given a copy of the policy, and then asked, “College coaches should never have sex with the student-athletes that they are coaching. True?” “I don’t know how to answer that,” Alberts replied. “I mean, you know, it just depends.” Alberts also said he tried not to pay attention to relationships. Considering the situation at Michigan with Sherrone Moore, maybe Alberts was not the right choice to begin with. top.title: Massachusetts high school football inks endorsement deal with New Balance
top.description: Massachusetts’ first five-star quarterback has signed his first endorsement deal with a Boston-based sportswear behemoth. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, New Balance released a commercial via Instagram officially unveiling St. John’s Prep junior Chris Vargas as a New Balance athlete. "Rooted in Boston. United by a love for the game," the company wrote in the caption. "We're proud to welcome local five-star quarterback prospect Chris Vargas to the New Balance family." Vargas, a Lawrence native who grew up a 10 minute drive from the company's factory in the city, said the feeling of earning an endorsement while still in high school was unbelieveable. "Just a small kid from Lawrence, Massachusetts, where Massachusetts isn't really like a big football state to play in... being a part of this New Balance family as a high school player is something that I'd never imagine would happen," Vargas said in the ad, which later shows him bringing New Balance cleats and signing autographs for Lawrence Pop Warner players, the place he says is "where it all began." The Ohio State commit , who highlights a crop of talented high school quarterbacks coming out of the Bay State , is having another monster season for the Eagles (11-0, 4-0 Catholic Conference), going 120-of-177 passing for 1,957 yards and 23 touchdowns while allowing just a pair of interceptions. On Oct. 30 in a Catholic Conference matchup with back-to-back MIAA Division 2 champions Catholic Memorial , Vargas went 12-of-21 passing for 203 yards and a pair of touchdowns to hand the Knights a 42-35 loss and secure the league title for the Danvers-based school. Vargas and the rest of the undefeated SJP squad have a pair of games remaining: first taking on arch-rivals Xaverian in their annual Thanksgiving showdown at home on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 7 p.m. before the top-seeded Eagles take on No. 2 St. John's Shrewsbury (10-1, 3-1 Catholic Conference) in the MIAA Division 1 Super Bowl at Boston College's Alumni Stadium on Saturday, Dec. 5, with an 11:30 a.m. kickoff scheduled. The Pioneers only loss of the year so far came against SJP on Oct. 16 , a 44-20 Eagles win in which Vargas tossed a pair of touchdown passes. top.title: Michigan's latest self-inflicted disaster proves yet again the Wolverines have a leadership problem
top.description: So let's make sure we have this straight. The University of Michigan, which has known since late July that outgoing athletic director Warde Manuel's last day would be Dec. 31, rushed to hire Trev Alberts as its new athletic director last week. The decision was made by incoming school president C. Cybele Raver, who hadn't even officially started yet but sped up the AD search so that Michigan could ostensibly fire football coach Kyle Whittingham and run a coaching search as quickly as possible. Then, upon agreeing to terms with Alberts, who resigned from his job at Texas A&M, Michigan learned through media reporting about Alberts' somewhat questionable comments from a deposition related to a human-resources issue two jobs ago at Nebraska. Because those comments were going to draw negative attention to Alberts, and Raver was going to have to answer some uncomfortable questions of her own to start her tenure, she decided to pull the plug on the whole deal and start over . A source with knowledge of the situation told Yahoo Sports that Raver made the decision to blow up the hire on her own over the objections of key regents, who had met over the weekend to discuss the deposition and approved the hire anyway. It's going to cost Michigan millions. It's going to have a major impact on urgent football decisions that probably shouldn't be made under these circumstances. It's going to make it exponentially harder for Michigan to hire a competent AD, which was already proving to be a challenge despite the amounts of money the school was throwing around. Other than that, great work Wolverines. Michigan won a football national title in 2023 and a men's basketball championship just seven months ago. Can you imagine what this school might be capable of with even somewhat competent leadership? Maybe one day, Michigan fans will be able to enjoy a stretch of years where they don't have to worry about a cheating scandal, criminal hackers as assistant coaches, recruiting violations or inappropriate relationships between coaches and employees. Unfortunately, that is not the era Michigan is in. Instead, it's an era of weak leadership, a politically motivated and meddlesome board of regents, and a university culture that doesn't seem to know what it wants to be. Trev Alberts previously worked as athletic director at Nebraska and Texas A&M. (Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) Steven Branscombe via Getty Images Now they've blown it up again — over, of all things, a guy trying to give a clinical answer in a deposition — and have become nothing less than the laughingstock of college sports. This is no way to run a big-time athletic department. And here's the worst part: Raver undoubtedly thinks she's doing the right thing. Though there's not a huge need to feel sorry for Alberts — one way or another, this career-altering misstep is going to result in millions of dollars hitting his bank account — this isn't the way to do business in college sports. top.title: 49ers fans took over Mexico City and turned it into a home game
top.description: Photo by Antonio Losada For the 2026 NFL season, the league decided to amplify its ever-expanding operation further, scheduling a record nine games outside the United States. As if the NFL needed any help growing its game, commissioner Roger Goodell got even luckier than he could have ever imagined and, for the international finale, set for Nov. 22 inside Estadio Banorte in Mexico City way before the season started, found himself stumbling into a premier matchup pitting the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers against a fellow contender from the NFC in the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings. Turns out, Mexico City wasn’t ready to allow any pesky Vikingo docking in the country to steal its Rojo y Oro . “I’m a fan since 1988. I was born in 1978. I’ve been following the team since I was 10, for nearly 40 years,” Alain Morales said. “I started watching Joe Montana sling the football even though my father rooted for San Francisco’s rivals. I wanted none of that.” Since I stepped into the biggest North American city for a third time in life, I could feel the 49ers Faithful presence everywhere. I had seen it from a distance before, but this time, I decided to start attending watch parties, talking to superfans from the official fan chapter , blending with them, and everything in between. They embraced and welcomed me from the get-go. I ended up participating in a Halloween costume party, cutting birthday cake gifted by someone I had never met, and eating pan de muerto with agua de jamaica . I first landed in Mexico City over a year ago, enthused and enticed from an ocean afar. Although my official 49ers rite of passage happened just a few moons ago at the start of my third time here, I had noticed something way before getting into the local Niners-catered scene rooted deep in Mexico’s soil. Step outside, and you’ll inevitably find tons of folks proudly wearing their Club América — the most-followed and winningest club in Liga MX, Mexico’s top-flight soccer league — jerseys. Look beyond, however, and you’ll notice big, oversized at times, red-and-white jerseys popping. No wonder San Francisco brought them. So for such a behemoth of an event as an NFL game in Mexico City, which last happened in 2022 and hadn’t happened since before COVID entered our lexicon, and featuring the team from The Bay, no less, you could rest assured the streets would be flooded with full-blown Niner aficionados , Mexican or not. “I’m originally from Miami, and I became a 49ers fan growing up watching Jerry Rice and watching them play, so I always cheer for them since I was six years old,” visiting Mike Brown said at the entrance to Estadio Banorte. “Now, I live in California, so I’m much more excited to be able to watch them every week. Puig isn't the only former LIV golfer set to tee it up in Sydney this week, either. Aussie Cam Smith is trying to win the BMW Australian PGA for the fourth time in his career, while 2024 champion Elvis Smylie and 2016 winner Harold Varner III look to regain the title. Several other former members of the breakaway circuit, like Marc Leishman, Michael La Sasso, Tom McKibbin, Josele Ballester, Ben An, Caleb Surratt and Thomas Pieters, will also compete. The PGA Tour will be well-represented, too, with the likes of two-time BMW Australian PGA winner Adam Scott, 2023 champion Min Woo Lee and 2008 champion Geoff Ogilvy set to tee it up in front of a home crowd, along with other Tour members such as Corey Conners, Alex Noren and Sudarshan Yellamaraju. top.title: Tigers agree on one-year deal with veteran infielder Ha-Seong Kim
top.description: DETROIT — It’s unusual for Tigers’ president Scott Harris to tip his hand, even a little bit. But during a press conference Tuesday, Nov. 24, to announce a six-year, $46.5 million extension for pitcher Troy Melton , he dropped a hint. “We’ve made some moves that haven’t been announced yet,” he said. “We are going to continue to add arms but we also want to protect those arms and make sure we tighten up our infield defense. We want to make sure we can translate soft contact into outs more effectively that we have recently.” To that end, the Tigers have reached an agreement with veteran infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year deal worth $5 million. The deal, which is pending medicals, was first reported by ESPN and confirmed to The Detroit News. Kim, 31, won a Gold Glove with the Padres in 2023, but he’s been injured the last two seasons, limited to 48 games with the Braves and Rays in 2025, and 51 games with the Braves last season. Still, although he only hit .161 in those 51 games, he was still a plus-4 defensive runs saved. He had shoulder surgery in 2025 and tore a tendon in his right middle finger last winter when he slipped on the ice back in South Korea. But the six-year veteran was healthy from the middle of July on last season, finishing the year with the Braves and playing in two playoff games. He can play shortstop, second base and third base and joins a mix that includes presumed regulars Kevin McGonigle (shortstop, third base), Javier Báez (shortstop, second base), Hao-Yu Lee (second base and third base) and Colt Keith (third base, first base), plus Tsung-Che Cheng (shortstop, second base), Max Anderson (second base) and John Peck (shortstop). top.title: Gabe Ouellette carries his family's Bristol football legacy into one last Battle for the Bell
top.description: Bristol Central senior Gabe Ouellette poses for a photo after a high school football practice on Nov. 19, 2026, in Bristol. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) BRISTOL - The name Ouellette has been synonymous with football in the Bell City since Gerry Ouellette played at Bristol Central in the mid-1980s. It's only fitting that the fifth and final member of the Ouellette family to play football in Bristol will suit up one last time on Thanksgiving morning in the annual Battle for the Bell. Gabe, the youngest of four brothers, is a senior quarterback for Bristol Central (4-5), which faces Bristol Eastern (1-8) at Muzzy Field at 10:30 a.m. "It feels crazy because I've grown up listening all about football," Gabe Ouellette said following practice on the Thursday before Thanksgiving. "My whole life has been football, to be able to watch great football players. There was a little bit of pressure, so I feel good that I was able to hold my own with them, but I'm happy about it. I'm happy about everything." The first Ouellette Gerard "Gerry" Ouellette, the father, ran for 1,335 yards in 1984, his senior season at Bristol Central. "You talk to some of the old-timers about their dad Gerry, it was the same thing (as the sons)," said current Central head coach Jeff Papazian, a quarterback for the Rams in the 1990s. "Not the biggest guy in the world, but played extremely hard and could run away from you and separate." Three Ouellettes, three Lancers Three of Gerry Ouellette's sons - Dylon, Tyler and Gerry III - played for Eastern. "The Ouellette brothers' time here at Bristol Eastern was defined by toughness. All three of them had that in common," said current Eastern head coach Anthony "AJ" Julius, who was an assistant coach when the brothers played for the Lancers. Dylon, 33, was the first Ouellette brother to play high school football in Bristol. In the 2010 Battle for the Bell, he ran for 208 yards on 18 carries and was named the team's offensive player of the game. That topped his father's mark of 189 yards on 18 carries in the 1984 game. Dylon also surpassed his father's season total with 1,391 yards in 2010. Eastern made the Class L state playoffs, losing at Masuk. Dylon graduated in 2011. Tyler, 31, also played for Eastern (Class of 2012), but his career was limited by two torn ACLs. "Tyler displayed great athletic ability but unfortunately was battling injuries a lot during his years here," Julius said. "He was a good teammate and hard worker. I have no doubt he would have been successful if not for injuries." Gabe agreed with Julius' assessment. "He probably would have been the best one, but he tore his ACL twice and gave it up," Ouellette said. "It was in the state championship game of an eighth-grade (Bristol) Bulldogs game, when he was carrying like three people. My dad said he tore his ACL." top.title: The Top 100 Cubs of all time, No. 87: Rogers Hornsby
top.description: Rogers Hornsby was one of the greatest MLB players ever. Of this, there is no doubt nor question. Rogers Hornsby was also one of the most disliked MLB players and managers ever — and there’s little doubt of that, too. Hornsby played 12 outstanding years for the Cardinals from 1915-26 and won the NL MVP award in 1925. He’d have won more of those if the award had existed prior to that, and the 1925 award was pre-BBWAA. He had five seasons of 10 or more bWAR in St. Louis and his 12.1 bWAR season in 1924, in which he batted .424/.507/.696, is one of the greatest MLB seasons ever. He was also the Cardinals’ manager in 1925 and 1926, and per his SABR biography he received “very high praise” for his managing abilities. Nevertheless, he wanted to renegotiate his contract, which had a year remaining, and Cardinals owner Sam Breadon got so frustrated with Hornsby that he traded him to the Giants. Hornsby lasted only one year there before being sent to the Braves and then, before the 1929 season, was traded to the Cubs for Bruce Cunningham, Percy Jones, Lou Legett, Freddie Maguire, Socks Seibold and $200,000. That was a tremendous sum of money in those days, roughly equivalent to $4 million today. The deal was made largely because the Braves were in financial trouble and needed the money badly. Hornsby immediately paid dividends on the field. You’ve probably heard a lot about his 1929 MVP season in comparison to Pete Crow-Armstrong’s great 2026 season, and in 1929 Hornsby batted .380/.459/.679 with 39 home runs, a league-leading 156 runs and 409 total bases, which to this day ranks fourth in Cubs history. That’s when things began to turn sour for Hornsby. He had a broken ankle in 1930 which limited him to just 42 games. The injury was one of the biggest reasons the Cubs didn’t repeat as NL champions in 1930, finishing just two games out of first place. And then Cubs owner William Wrigley made a decision that was franchise-altering. From the SABR bio: Cubs owner William Wrigley had become disenchanted with Joe McCarthy and announced with four games left in the season that Hornsby would take over as player-manager for 1931. Although there were rumors that Hornsby had undermined McCarthy and actively sought his job, the Rajah denied it, saying the two had parted as friends. Others, like teammates Gabby Hartnett and Charlie Grimm, were not convinced. Cubs president William Veeck, Sr. was so upset at Hornsby’s hiring that he resigned, only to come back when Wrigley promised he would never interfere again. Veeck put up with what has been characterized as Hornsby’s “reign of terror” for about a season and a half before firing him on August 2, 1932. In the interim Hornsby had gotten cross-ways with just about everyone on the team, including stars like Gabby Hartnett, Hack Wilson, Kiki Cuyler, and Billy Herman. top.title: Survey: Will the Giants put it all together against the Colts?
top.description: ﻿The New York Giants offense huddles before a play | Getty Images The New York Giants are riding high after — once again — coming up with a win as underdogs. Very few people thought the Giants would beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are widely considered among the best and most complete teams in the NFL. The most optimistic among us believed that there was a path for the Giants to come up with the win, but weren’t sure if they could execute. As it turned out, they did. They were able to do just enough on offense to establish a lead while their defense turned in a dominant performance for most of the game. It was a great game by the Giants, but it wasn’t a complete game. The offense was still inconsistent and plagued by turnovers, miscues, and penalties. And while the defense was able to pick them up, they were gassed by the end of the game because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive after Cam Skattebo’s fumble. The Giants’ win over the Jags is proving to be even bigger than anticipated, with the rest of the NFC East winning as well. That makes the upcoming game against the Indianapolis Colts into much more of a “must win” than it was before the Washington Commanders’ upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals. This is the time for the Giants to begin peaking if they want to be competitive in their upcoming games against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions. So this week we want to ask the Big Blue View community: Can the Giants put it all together and play a complete game against the Colts? Your choices this week are: A) Yes – The Giants’ offense and defense will play a complete 60 minute of football against the Colts. B) No – The mistakes and miscues will return, but there will be marked improvement over previous weeks. C) No – The offense is too mistake prone, with too many new players (J.J. top.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
top.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. nigeria.title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The event attracted supporters from the 14 local government areas of the state, including party faithful, women and youth groups, traditional leaders and other political stakeholders. Addressing the gathering, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said voting for the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the state Houses of Assembly, would enable the state to benefit from federal government projects, appointments and other interventions. He argued that Zamfara could not afford to remain in opposition in 2027, urging residents to align with the ruling party at the federal level. “I urge you, the good people of Zamfara, to vote for APC from top to bottom in 2027. Vote for President Tinubu, vote for Governor Lawal, vote for our senators, House of Representatives members and State Assembly members. That is the only way Zamfara will move forward,” Yari said. He also urged voters to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the President as the candidate capable of driving development in the North-West and the country. Yari said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated commitment to addressing insecurity, reviving the economy, improving infrastructure and repositioning the country for sustainable growth. He noted that the North-West, which had experienced years of banditry, kidnapping and economic challenges, needed sustained investment in security and development. “President Tinubu is the only candidate who, if given a second mandate, will develop the North-West and the country at large. He has the vision, the experience and the political will to take Nigeria to the next level. We must give him our full support,” he said. Yari called on Zamfara residents to give Tinubu substantial electoral support in 2027, as they did in 2023, to enable him to complete his reform agenda. He also canvassed support for Governor Lawal’s second-term ambition, saying the governor needed the backing of residents to consolidate his administration’s Rescue Zamfara Agenda. According to him, cooperation between the Federal Government and the Zamfara State Government would accelerate development in security, job creation, education, healthcare and infrastructure. The campaign launch was attended by APC stakeholders, government officials, members of the state executive council, federal and state lawmakers, local government chairmen, women and youth groups, and party supporters. nigeria.title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat. The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area. Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed. The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations. The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North. Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party. “The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none. “We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.” He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled. The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements. Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex. He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas. nigeria.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65% UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country. The six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit said in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026. The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported . How the certificate works A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself. If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years. That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default. “With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit. “Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.” Built on notes sold in Germany and Austria Di Stasi said the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20% South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups issue won stablecoins. The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users. Lee said the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted quickly. A 20% ownership cap for exchanges Under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market. Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. Existing exchanges would get three years after designation to comply, and small and midsize exchanges could get up to three more. The cap could reach some of Korea’s best-known exchanges. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move. The complaint , filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft. On Nov. 12, the department said it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day. Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds. Circle will mint replacement tokens Circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control. Instead, Circle has agreed to issue new USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.” Several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint says. How the Binance hack worked The filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange said earlier this month. The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors said the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Relai Launches Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Plans by Goal Swiss bitcoin app Relai launched Stacks on Tuesday, a feature that lets users run several recurring bitcoin savings plans side by side, one for each goal, such as a house, a wedding or a child’s first car. Stacks is live for all Relai users in Switzerland and the European Union. Each Stack carries its own amount and schedule, and users can change either at any time without starting over, the company said. A savings plan is Relai’s version of dollar-cost averaging: buying a fixed amount of bitcoin on a set schedule, weekly or monthly, regardless of price. Savers use it to avoid timing the market. Since September, Relai users have been able to change the amount and buy date of an active plan. Stacks applies that to several goals at once, so a saver can put more toward a house one month, slow down a car fund the next and leave an emergency reserve untouched. In practice, Stacks is an organizing layer, not a new account. Relai’s help pages describe each Stack as a separate pot with its own bitcoin address inside the same wallet. Users get up to five custom Stacks plus a main balance, and moving bitcoin between them takes a regular on-chain transaction with a network fee. Self-custody cuts both ways Relai is self-custodial, meaning it does not hold customers’ bitcoin. The coins in every Stack sit in a wallet controlled by a 12-word recovery phrase, or seed phrase, that only the user has. All Stacks share that one phrase, and restoring the wallet with it brings every Stack back. The trade-off is responsibility. A saver who loses the phrase and the phone has no password reset and no support desk that can recover the coins. Anyone who gets the phrase can take them, which is why attackers have gone as far as tampering with hardware wallets to capture it. “Everyone saves for something. A home, their kids, the freedom to stop working one day,” said Julian Liniger, Relai’s co-founder and CEO. “With Stacks, you can save for each of those goals in Bitcoin, at your own pace.” How Relai is regulated In the EU, Relai’s French unit is authorized by France’s financial markets regulator, the AMF, as a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, the bloc’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation . Relai secured that license in October 2025, and under MiCA a firm licensed in one member state can “passport” its services across the bloc. Swiss and Liechtenstein customers are served by Relai AG, which is affiliated with VQF , a self-regulatory organization recognized by Swiss regulator FINMA under the country’s anti-money laundering law. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. Through this film, Kevin Hart shares his vision of what it means to be a man and a father. The film reveals the journey of a young boy on the brink of adulthood, revealing the pressures of identity and self-definition. There is a lot to unpack from Stephen Graham’ s Adolescence about what it means to be a father and a child. King Richard A faction. sports.title: The story that ended Trev Alberts’ Michigan AD tenure before it even began
sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-USA TODAY Sports The story that ended Trev Alberts’ Michigan AD tenure before it even began appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michigan has decided not to hire Trev Alberts as the next athletic director. Michigan reversed course on the hire on Tuesday , even though there was a memorandum of understanding signed between the two sides. Now, the story that ended the Alberts’ tenure before it even began has come to light. David Covucci of FOIAball found a lawsuit that involved Trev Alberts, who was then the Nebraska AD. The lawsuit was filed in 2024 by Ashley Scoggin against the Nebraska Board of Regents, the school’s women’s basketball coach, and then-AD Alberts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “According to the lawsuit, during an away game, a student-manager duped a hotel employee into giving out a card key to assistant coach Chuck Love’s room. Two players used the card to enter Love’s room and filmed Scoggin in his bed. Presented with the video, head coach Amy Williams allegedly called a meeting and allowed the entire team to confront Scoggin over the relationship,” Covucci wrote. “Scoggin was initially suspended. Back in Nebraska, she was kicked off the team. Love was suspended with pay and allowed to quietly resign three months later. Alberts eventually agreed to pay Love $136,000 in severance. The lawsuit accuses Alberts of violating Scoggin’s civil rights after learning of the relationship by approving of her removal from the team, refusing to order an investigation, and encouraging her to leave the school.” The lawsuit led to two different depositions of Alberts, and some shocking details from the depositions came to light. First, he did not know he had been named vice chancellor at Nebraska. Meanwhile, he also gave some evasive answers about relationships between staff and students. “Faculty or Staff members are prohibited from engaging in any romantic relationship with an undergraduate student,” the Nebraska policy on consensual relationships reads. Alberts was given a copy of the policy, and then asked, “College coaches should never have sex with the student-athletes that they are coaching. True?” “I don’t know how to answer that,” Alberts replied. “I mean, you know, it just depends.” Alberts also said he tried not to pay attention to relationships. Considering the situation at Michigan with Sherrone Moore, maybe Alberts was not the right choice to begin with. sports.title: Massachusetts high school football inks endorsement deal with New Balance
sports.description: Massachusetts’ first five-star quarterback has signed his first endorsement deal with a Boston-based sportswear behemoth. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, New Balance released a commercial via Instagram officially unveiling St. John’s Prep junior Chris Vargas as a New Balance athlete. "Rooted in Boston. United by a love for the game," the company wrote in the caption. "We're proud to welcome local five-star quarterback prospect Chris Vargas to the New Balance family." Vargas, a Lawrence native who grew up a 10 minute drive from the company's factory in the city, said the feeling of earning an endorsement while still in high school was unbelieveable. "Just a small kid from Lawrence, Massachusetts, where Massachusetts isn't really like a big football state to play in... being a part of this New Balance family as a high school player is something that I'd never imagine would happen," Vargas said in the ad, which later shows him bringing New Balance cleats and signing autographs for Lawrence Pop Warner players, the place he says is "where it all began." The Ohio State commit , who highlights a crop of talented high school quarterbacks coming out of the Bay State , is having another monster season for the Eagles (11-0, 4-0 Catholic Conference), going 120-of-177 passing for 1,957 yards and 23 touchdowns while allowing just a pair of interceptions. On Oct. 30 in a Catholic Conference matchup with back-to-back MIAA Division 2 champions Catholic Memorial , Vargas went 12-of-21 passing for 203 yards and a pair of touchdowns to hand the Knights a 42-35 loss and secure the league title for the Danvers-based school. Vargas and the rest of the undefeated SJP squad have a pair of games remaining: first taking on arch-rivals Xaverian in their annual Thanksgiving showdown at home on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 7 p.m. before the top-seeded Eagles take on No. 2 St. John's Shrewsbury (10-1, 3-1 Catholic Conference) in the MIAA Division 1 Super Bowl at Boston College's Alumni Stadium on Saturday, Dec. 5, with an 11:30 a.m. kickoff scheduled. The Pioneers only loss of the year so far came against SJP on Oct. 16 , a 44-20 Eagles win in which Vargas tossed a pair of touchdown passes. sports.title: Michigan's latest self-inflicted disaster proves yet again the Wolverines have a leadership problem
sports.description: So let's make sure we have this straight. The University of Michigan, which has known since late July that outgoing athletic director Warde Manuel's last day would be Dec. 31, rushed to hire Trev Alberts as its new athletic director last week. The decision was made by incoming school president C. Cybele Raver, who hadn't even officially started yet but sped up the AD search so that Michigan could ostensibly fire football coach Kyle Whittingham and run a coaching search as quickly as possible. Then, upon agreeing to terms with Alberts, who resigned from his job at Texas A&M, Michigan learned through media reporting about Alberts' somewhat questionable comments from a deposition related to a human-resources issue two jobs ago at Nebraska. Because those comments were going to draw negative attention to Alberts, and Raver was going to have to answer some uncomfortable questions of her own to start her tenure, she decided to pull the plug on the whole deal and start over . A source with knowledge of the situation told Yahoo Sports that Raver made the decision to blow up the hire on her own over the objections of key regents, who had met over the weekend to discuss the deposition and approved the hire anyway. It's going to cost Michigan millions. It's going to have a major impact on urgent football decisions that probably shouldn't be made under these circumstances. It's going to make it exponentially harder for Michigan to hire a competent AD, which was already proving to be a challenge despite the amounts of money the school was throwing around. Other than that, great work Wolverines. Michigan won a football national title in 2023 and a men's basketball championship just seven months ago. Can you imagine what this school might be capable of with even somewhat competent leadership? Maybe one day, Michigan fans will be able to enjoy a stretch of years where they don't have to worry about a cheating scandal, criminal hackers as assistant coaches, recruiting violations or inappropriate relationships between coaches and employees. Unfortunately, that is not the era Michigan is in. Instead, it's an era of weak leadership, a politically motivated and meddlesome board of regents, and a university culture that doesn't seem to know what it wants to be. Trev Alberts previously worked as athletic director at Nebraska and Texas A&M. (Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) Steven Branscombe via Getty Images Now they've blown it up again — over, of all things, a guy trying to give a clinical answer in a deposition — and have become nothing less than the laughingstock of college sports. This is no way to run a big-time athletic department. And here's the worst part: Raver undoubtedly thinks she's doing the right thing. sports.title: 49ers fans took over Mexico City and turned it into a home game
sports.description: Photo by Antonio Losada For the 2026 NFL season, the league decided to amplify its ever-expanding operation further, scheduling a record nine games outside the United States. As if the NFL needed any help growing its game, commissioner Roger Goodell got even luckier than he could have ever imagined and, for the international finale, set for Nov. 22 inside Estadio Banorte in Mexico City way before the season started, found himself stumbling into a premier matchup pitting the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers against a fellow contender from the NFC in the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings. Turns out, Mexico City wasn’t ready to allow any pesky Vikingo docking in the country to steal its Rojo y Oro . “I’m a fan since 1988. I was born in 1978. I’ve been following the team since I was 10, for nearly 40 years,” Alain Morales said. “I started watching Joe Montana sling the football even though my father rooted for San Francisco’s rivals. I wanted none of that.” Since I stepped into the biggest North American city for a third time in life, I could feel the 49ers Faithful presence everywhere. I had seen it from a distance before, but this time, I decided to start attending watch parties, talking to superfans from the official fan chapter , blending with them, and everything in between. They embraced and welcomed me from the get-go. I ended up participating in a Halloween costume party, cutting birthday cake gifted by someone I had never met, and eating pan de muerto with agua de jamaica . I first landed in Mexico City over a year ago, enthused and enticed from an ocean afar. Although my official 49ers rite of passage happened just a few moons ago at the start of my third time here, I had noticed something way before getting into the local Niners-catered scene rooted deep in Mexico’s soil. Step outside, and you’ll inevitably find tons of folks proudly wearing their Club América — the most-followed and winningest club in Liga MX, Mexico’s top-flight soccer league — jerseys. Look beyond, however, and you’ll notice big, oversized at times, red-and-white jerseys popping. No wonder San Francisco brought them. So for such a behemoth of an event as an NFL game in Mexico City, which last happened in 2022 and hadn’t happened since before COVID entered our lexicon, and featuring the team from The Bay, no less, you could rest assured the streets would be flooded with full-blown Niner aficionados , Mexican or not. “I’m originally from Miami, and I became a 49ers fan growing up watching Jerry Rice and watching them play, so I always cheer for them since I was six years old,” visiting Mike Brown said at the entrance to Estadio Banorte. “Now, I live in California, so I’m much more excited to be able to watch them every week. sports.title: Tigers agree on one-year deal with veteran infielder Ha-Seong Kim
sports.description: DETROIT — It’s unusual for Tigers’ president Scott Harris to tip his hand, even a little bit. But during a press conference Tuesday, Nov. 24, to announce a six-year, $46.5 million extension for pitcher Troy Melton , he dropped a hint. “We’ve made some moves that haven’t been announced yet,” he said. “We are going to continue to add arms but we also want to protect those arms and make sure we tighten up our infield defense. We want to make sure we can translate soft contact into outs more effectively that we have recently.” To that end, the Tigers have reached an agreement with veteran infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year deal worth $5 million. The deal, which is pending medicals, was first reported by ESPN and confirmed to The Detroit News. Kim, 31, won a Gold Glove with the Padres in 2023, but he’s been injured the last two seasons, limited to 48 games with the Braves and Rays in 2025, and 51 games with the Braves last season. Still, although he only hit .161 in those 51 games, he was still a plus-4 defensive runs saved. He had shoulder surgery in 2025 and tore a tendon in his right middle finger last winter when he slipped on the ice back in South Korea. But the six-year veteran was healthy from the middle of July on last season, finishing the year with the Braves and playing in two playoff games. He can play shortstop, second base and third base and joins a mix that includes presumed regulars Kevin McGonigle (shortstop, third base), Javier Báez (shortstop, second base), Hao-Yu Lee (second base and third base) and Colt Keith (third base, first base), plus Tsung-Che Cheng (shortstop, second base), Max Anderson (second base) and John Peck (shortstop). sports.title: Gabe Ouellette carries his family's Bristol football legacy into one last Battle for the Bell
sports.description: Bristol Central senior Gabe Ouellette poses for a photo after a high school football practice on Nov. 19, 2026, in Bristol. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) BRISTOL - The name Ouellette has been synonymous with football in the Bell City since Gerry Ouellette played at Bristol Central in the mid-1980s. It's only fitting that the fifth and final member of the Ouellette family to play football in Bristol will suit up one last time on Thanksgiving morning in the annual Battle for the Bell. Gabe, the youngest of four brothers, is a senior quarterback for Bristol Central (4-5), which faces Bristol Eastern (1-8) at Muzzy Field at 10:30 a.m. "It feels crazy because I've grown up listening all about football," Gabe Ouellette said following practice on the Thursday before Thanksgiving. "My whole life has been football, to be able to watch great football players. There was a little bit of pressure, so I feel good that I was able to hold my own with them, but I'm happy about it. I'm happy about everything." The first Ouellette Gerard "Gerry" Ouellette, the father, ran for 1,335 yards in 1984, his senior season at Bristol Central. "You talk to some of the old-timers about their dad Gerry, it was the same thing (as the sons)," said current Central head coach Jeff Papazian, a quarterback for the Rams in the 1990s. "Not the biggest guy in the world, but played extremely hard and could run away from you and separate." Three Ouellettes, three Lancers Three of Gerry Ouellette's sons - Dylon, Tyler and Gerry III - played for Eastern. "The Ouellette brothers' time here at Bristol Eastern was defined by toughness. All three of them had that in common," said current Eastern head coach Anthony "AJ" Julius, who was an assistant coach when the brothers played for the Lancers. Dylon, 33, was the first Ouellette brother to play high school football in Bristol. In the 2010 Battle for the Bell, he ran for 208 yards on 18 carries and was named the team's offensive player of the game. That topped his father's mark of 189 yards on 18 carries in the 1984 game. Dylon also surpassed his father's season total with 1,391 yards in 2010. Eastern made the Class L state playoffs, losing at Masuk. Dylon graduated in 2011. Tyler, 31, also played for Eastern (Class of 2012), but his career was limited by two torn ACLs. "Tyler displayed great athletic ability but unfortunately was battling injuries a lot during his years here," Julius said. "He was a good teammate and hard worker. I have no doubt he would have been successful if not for injuries." Gabe agreed with Julius' assessment. "He probably would have been the best one, but he tore his ACL twice and gave it up," Ouellette said. "It was in the state championship game of an eighth-grade (Bristol) Bulldogs game, when he was carrying like three people. My dad said he tore his ACL." sports.title: The Top 100 Cubs of all time, No. 87: Rogers Hornsby
sports.description: Rogers Hornsby was one of the greatest MLB players ever. Of this, there is no doubt nor question. Rogers Hornsby was also one of the most disliked MLB players and managers ever — and there’s little doubt of that, too. Hornsby played 12 outstanding years for the Cardinals from 1915-26 and won the NL MVP award in 1925. He’d have won more of those if the award had existed prior to that, and the 1925 award was pre-BBWAA. He had five seasons of 10 or more bWAR in St. Louis and his 12.1 bWAR season in 1924, in which he batted .424/.507/.696, is one of the greatest MLB seasons ever. He was also the Cardinals’ manager in 1925 and 1926, and per his SABR biography he received “very high praise” for his managing abilities. Nevertheless, he wanted to renegotiate his contract, which had a year remaining, and Cardinals owner Sam Breadon got so frustrated with Hornsby that he traded him to the Giants. Hornsby lasted only one year there before being sent to the Braves and then, before the 1929 season, was traded to the Cubs for Bruce Cunningham, Percy Jones, Lou Legett, Freddie Maguire, Socks Seibold and $200,000. That was a tremendous sum of money in those days, roughly equivalent to $4 million today. The deal was made largely because the Braves were in financial trouble and needed the money badly. Hornsby immediately paid dividends on the field. You’ve probably heard a lot about his 1929 MVP season in comparison to Pete Crow-Armstrong’s great 2026 season, and in 1929 Hornsby batted .380/.459/.679 with 39 home runs, a league-leading 156 runs and 409 total bases, which to this day ranks fourth in Cubs history. That’s when things began to turn sour for Hornsby. He had a broken ankle in 1930 which limited him to just 42 games. The injury was one of the biggest reasons the Cubs didn’t repeat as NL champions in 1930, finishing just two games out of first place. And then Cubs owner William Wrigley made a decision that was franchise-altering. From the SABR bio: Cubs owner William Wrigley had become disenchanted with Joe McCarthy and announced with four games left in the season that Hornsby would take over as player-manager for 1931. Although there were rumors that Hornsby had undermined McCarthy and actively sought his job, the Rajah denied it, saying the two had parted as friends. Others, like teammates Gabby Hartnett and Charlie Grimm, were not convinced. Cubs president William Veeck, Sr. was so upset at Hornsby’s hiring that he resigned, only to come back when Wrigley promised he would never interfere again. Veeck put up with what has been characterized as Hornsby’s “reign of terror” for about a season and a half before firing him on August 2, 1932. In the interim Hornsby had gotten cross-ways with just about everyone on the team, including stars like Gabby Hartnett, Hack Wilson, Kiki Cuyler, and Billy Herman. sports.title: Survey: Will the Giants put it all together against the Colts?
sports.description: ﻿The New York Giants offense huddles before a play | Getty Images The New York Giants are riding high after — once again — coming up with a win as underdogs. Very few people thought the Giants would beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are widely considered among the best and most complete teams in the NFL. The most optimistic among us believed that there was a path for the Giants to come up with the win, but weren’t sure if they could execute. As it turned out, they did. They were able to do just enough on offense to establish a lead while their defense turned in a dominant performance for most of the game. It was a great game by the Giants, but it wasn’t a complete game. The offense was still inconsistent and plagued by turnovers, miscues, and penalties. And while the defense was able to pick them up, they were gassed by the end of the game because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive after Cam Skattebo’s fumble. The Giants’ win over the Jags is proving to be even bigger than anticipated, with the rest of the NFC East winning as well. That makes the upcoming game against the Indianapolis Colts into much more of a “must win” than it was before the Washington Commanders’ upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals. This is the time for the Giants to begin peaking if they want to be competitive in their upcoming games against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions. So this week we want to ask the Big Blue View community: Can the Giants put it all together and play a complete game against the Colts? Your choices this week are: A) Yes – The Giants’ offense and defense will play a complete 60 minute of football against the Colts. sports.title: A Path To A Better Bullpen
sports.description: Relief pitcher Brandyn Garcia (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inspiration . The Diamondbacks bullpen was the best it’s been in years. But of the 29 Diamondbacks who pitched in relief, more than half are no longer on the Diamondbacks roster. Will acquisition of relief pitchers be impacted by the expectation that next season’s team salary will be less than this season? Data from Baseball Reference, Spotrac, and FanGraphs. Which relief pitchers will be back next season? Following are two tables: the first shows pitchers who are currently gone, and the second shows pitchers who are likely to return next season. Each table shows relief pitchers, their unadjusted cash salary for their relief appearances (rounded to the nearest $100,000), their age, their estimated bWAR earned in relief, were they with the Dbacks in 2025, and if they are gone, what happened. Note that the names of returning relievers are in purple text. There are 10 relief pitchers who remain on the roster (and one of the ten is catcher Adrian Del Castillo who may on rare occasion pitch in relief next season). They earned a total of $5.4 Million while earning 4.4 bWAR. In addition, their average age is 26.1 years old (Baseball Reference age for 2026 season). That compares well with the average of 31.0 years old for those taken off the roster. For two reasons (excellent performance by the retained relievers and the retained relievers were younger), the retained relief pitchers are a great core to build around for next season. However, the retained relief pitchers will not be enough. In total, they pitched 33% of the relief innings. Even if they increased their innings pitched by 50%, they will cover only half the needed innings. Additional relief pitchers will be needed. How much will Diamondbacks spend on relief pitchers? In 2023, when the Diamondbacks reached the playoffs, and again in 2026, the bullpen’s share of the total adjusted payroll was 12%. Perhaps 12% is the optimal bullpen spending to maximize team wins. Preserving 12% is important in the context of the possible reduction of the team payroll. The following quote about team payroll was key to my understanding. “It will not be at the same level; It will be a lower payroll than we had last year….We have some significant contracts that are expiring with, unfortunately, players who made little or no contributions to the team.” — Ken Kendricks, Managing General Partner of the Diamondbacks, interviewed by Burns & Gambo, Arizona Sports My assumption is that 12% will be spent on the bullpen next season. A few players improved the team by leaving, so the team will improve without the need to spend what they were paid last season. If that idea accounted for 100% of the anticipated reduction in next season total salary, then it makes sense. It’s noteworthy that the turnover of relief pitchers increased. sports.title: Daniel Cormier warns Navajo Stirling if he’s unwilling to fight teammate Carlos Ulberg, then Alex Pereira can get ‘title fight right away’
sports.description: Alex Pereira is a two-time light heavyweight champion | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC Daniel Cormier understands the conundrum Navajo Stirling and Carlos Ulberg are currently dealing with. Stirling scored an impressive knockout over Jiri Prochazka in this past Saturday’s UFC Qatar main event to remain undefeated and leave little doubt that he is a top contender at 205 pounds, arguably No. 1. However, Ulberg, the current champion of the division, just so happens to be Stirling’s friend and teammate, and the two have been reluctant to commit to a potential matchup. Matchmakers are unlikely to make a decision on the matter anytime soon, but the situation could become more urgent if two-time light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira returns to the division. Pereira vacated his title to commit to chasing gold at heavyweight, but if he loses to Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335, it could prompt a move back to the division he previously conquered, especially if an immediate title shot awaits. “If Alex Pereira loses, he goes down, I think he gets a title fight right away,” Cormier said on his YouTube channel. “Nobody goes before Pereira if it doesn’t work out at heavyweight. Pereira gets a title fight right away, but [Dominick] Reyes, [Paulo] Costa, both, [Magomed] Ankalaev, all three of those guys are very tough. “It feels like to me, lately, the wins from these guys, they don’t match up to what Navajo’s done, because Costa beat the kid that Reyes beat last, before, and again, they’re not former champions. I think Navajo Stirling’s the No. 1 contender right now.” Following his win, Stirling told reporters, “We’ll cross that bridge” when the time comes for there to be serious talks about him fighting Ulberg, who is currently on the shelf dealing with a knee injury suffered in his own win over Prochazka for the vacant belt this past April. Before knocking Prochazka out, Ulberg tore his ACL, an injury that is likely to keep him out of action until at least early 2027. Cormier sympathizes with Stirling deferring to Ulberg, because he was in a similar position with heavyweight star Cain Velasquez when Cormier joined the UFC in 2013. “I lived in this situation with Cain Velasquez,” Cormier said. “When I got to [American Kickboxing Academy], I was the Olympic wrestler coming into a division with the heavyweight champ. It was so far down the road that you don’t think about it, but now Navajo Stirling is right at the doorstep of a UFC title shot.” Cormier initially dropped down to light heavyweight, where he eventually became champion and repeated that feat at heavyweight with Velasquez later out of the picture. sports.description: Free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe The New York Yankees could use some help in the infield, and there are still some solid options available. Jazz Chisholm Jr. was not good at second base last year, and he could be playing elsewhere next year. Ryan McMahon has been a disaster of an addition at third base, at least offensively. The Yankees are pretty much set in the outfield and have some internal options to play at second and third base, but adding upgrades should be seen as a priority. The Yankees could just target a third baseman and use Luis Garcia Jr. and Anthony Volpe at second base. However, Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer predicted the Yankees would go big and add Brandon Lowe and Casey Schmitt. Lowe is a clear fit for the Yankees. He is a great player at the plate and could post even better numbers at Yankee Stadium. He was also a great defender at second base last season. Schmitt could be the Yankees' fix at third base. He is a versatile defender who can play at third base for the Yankees. The San Francisco Giants are reportedly willing to trade him for pitching help. The Yankees could offer Will Warren and perhaps throw in Anthony Volpe. Volpe would not really be needed if the Yankees add Lowe. Schmitt had a .784 OPS last season, but his path to regular playing time in San Francisco is unclear. Adding both Lowe and Schmitt complicates things for Garcia, but the Yankees should still be able to find him at-bats. More MLB: Is Paul Goldschmidt Enough To Fix Mets' First Base Problems?

sports.title: 'I do feel pressure': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opens up after record-breaking double century
sports.description: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have rewritten the List A record books with a breathtaking 53-ball double century, but the teenager revealed that there was no change in his mindset going into the record-breaking innings against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday. The 15-year-old smashed an astonishing 204 off just 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes, the most ever by a batter in List A cricket, as India A chased down UAE's 250-run target in just 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets in their Group B encounter in Doha. Sooryavanshi registered the fastest century and double century in List A cricket, reaching the 100-run milestone in just 28 balls before completing his double hundred off 52 deliveries. He also became the first batter to score two List A half-centuries in 16 balls or fewer. Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Sooryavanshi explained that his approach was initially to spend time at the crease after failing to convert his starts in the previous two matches. However, he quickly realised that the surface offered little assistance to the bowlers and decided to back his natural attacking game. "In the last two matches, I got set but couldn't convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren't getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths," Sooryavanshi said. The left-hander revealed that his focus was simply on assessing the conditions and adjusting his approach accordingly, rather than thinking about records or milestones. "There wasn't anything specific on my mind. The only thought was that if the wicket was helping the bowlers, I would take my time and play a longer innings. But thankfully, that wasn't the case. The wicket was good, the ball was coming nicely onto the bat, so I tried to back my game," he added. 'Same mindset of trying to bat deep' Despite producing one of the most extraordinary innings in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi insisted that his mindset remained unchanged. He said his priority was always to bat deep and take control of the game once he settled in. "Nothing different, sir. It was the same mindset of trying to bat deep. If the game wasn't in my control initially, I would look to take my time. But thankfully, I was able to take control early on, and then I played the game on my terms," he said. Sooryavanshi also spoke about his experience of captaining Bihar, describing it as an enjoyable responsibility. He credited the senior players around him for making the environment comfortable and encouraging open discussions within the team. Chimere Dike Dike seems to be filling Wan'Dale Robinson's slot role in the Titans offense. He ran 60% of his routes from the slot in Week 11. Dike's route rate was 73%, the second-best on the team. In 2026, his sample size is small, but Dike has caught 19 of 22 targets for 209 yards and 1 touchdown. He has zero drops, and when Cam Ward is targeting Dike, he has a 121.4 passer rating. Konata Mumpfield With Puka Nacua newly out for the season, Mumpfield became the WR1 in Week 10. He ran a 96% route rate with a stellar 3.24 Yards per Route Run. Unlike other wide receivers, Bateman could catch just three passes to be a WR3 in fantasy football, and four might make him a WR2. Not much is required for relevance here, and if Zay Flowers or Ja'Kobi Lane were to get hurt, the ceiling would rise even higher.
